newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Commercial Bank warned by central bank.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Bank warned by central bank.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea (BOK) has issued a warning to Commercial Bank of Korea for extending improper loans to the collapsed Sammi Corp, a central bank statement said on Friday.
The warning, which came in BOK's annual bank inspection report, held the bank responsible for giving loans to Sammi even after the company was experiencing financial trouble.
Commercial Bank was the prime creditor of Sammi Corp which collapsed in March.
The central bank also urged Commercial Bank to pay more attention to managing financially troubled companies and implement careful credit analysis.

Despite the warning, the central bank said the Commercial Bank of Korea's weighted bad loan ratio dropped to 1.34 percent at the end of 1996 against 2.81 percent a year ago, and its non-performing loan ratio fell to 4.38 percent from 9.94 percent.
The commercial bank's net profit rose to 105.5 billion won in 1996 from 91.6 billion won a year before.
Its total assets increased to 41.9 trillion won by the end of February, compared with 35.1 trillion a year earlier.
